They like to use ingredients from the region, but international influences can also be detected on the menu. The service is professional and very attentive. They also have guestrooms.

Name: Gasthaus Hofmann
Description: It is no wonder that this inn run by Bettina Hofmann attracts so many regulars – diners are won over by the cosy, elegantly furnished interior, as well as the exceptional food. Her appetising cuisine is regional, seasonal and dotted with modern influences, and the wines are excellent. In addition, they serve a vegetarian set menu. The service is friendly and well organised. There are also comfortable guestrooms. The eggs served at breakfast are laid by the establishment's own hens!

Name: Jägerwirt
Description: With its cosy rustic-style interior, charming service and down-to-earth, flavoursome cuisine, this is the archetypal Bavarian inn at its best. The menu features regional dishes and Mediterranean-influenced options. The chefs make a point of sourcing their ingredients locally and work with trusted producers. Alongside the standard menu, there is a varying menu of the day plus a weekly special. Popular grilled veal and pork hock dishes, as well as goose and duck, are also available if ordered in advance. The rural location is also delightful.

Name: derWaldfrieden
Description: Run by the Hupfer family, this establishment enjoys a tranquil location on the Herrenschwand high plateau, 1 020m above sea level. This stunning setting is surrounded by an abundance of greenery – unsurprisingly, tables on the garden terrace are coveted. Son Volker delivers exceptional cuisine that is entirely centered on the region and the season. In addition to set menus (regular or vegan) and à la carte dishes, there is a selection of traditional Black Forest snacks. Overnight accommodation in this picturesque corner of Todtnau can easily be arranged – guestrooms are available in stammHaus and spaHaus.

Name: Gasthof zur Sonne
Description: This charming traditional inn with its striking red façade may be a little off the beaten track, but the flavoursome regional and Mediterranean cuisine served here makes the journey worthwhile. Be sure to set aside some time because Egbert Tribelhorn is the sole chef at work here, and he takes great pride in the quality and meticulous preparation of his creations. Your patience will be rewarded with impeccably crafted and bold classic dishes. Diners often opt for the "Sonnen-Menü" set menu, but the à la carte options are also very popular. The house-made ravioli are a must-try.The restaurant also has three simple but beautifully kept guestrooms.

Name: Forst's Landhaus
Description: Run with great dedication, this restaurant is located by a small stream – tables on the terrace overlooking the water are in great demand! The seasonal menu uses plenty of regional produce, such as lamb from the Bavarian Jura. The vegetarian dishes are also appealing, imaginative and delicious! The friendly maître d' provides good service with a personal touch. There are simple but well-kept guestrooms for overnight stays.

Name: Gasthof Berghof - Ursprung
Description: "Tradition meets modernity" is the theme here when it comes to both the decor and the flavoursome cuisine, which emphasises seasonal produce. The menu tempts diners with barbecued specialities and classics such as Franconian Fleckvieh beef roulade, or pike-perch fillet on a bed of creamed sauerkraut, not forgetting the Kaiserschmarrn (shredded pancake) with vanilla ice cream and apple compote. Be sure to take advantage of the inviting courtyard terrace in summer! For overnight stays, there are well-kept guestrooms and a lovely modern holiday home.

Name: Klösterle Hof
Description: Chef Markus Klein and his wife put their heart and soul into running this restaurant. In a spruce rustic-style decor – or out on the lovely terrace in summer – friendly waitstaff serve up delicious regional and seasonal cuisine made using good-quality ingredients. House specialties include golden trout and brown trout, sourced from Lohmühle trout farm in Alpirsbach. Good to know: Hot meals are served from noon to 8pm. Tip for overnight guests: Ask for the "Wohlfühl" or "Komfort" guestrooms.

Name: Gehrlein's Hardtwald
Description: Somewhat tucked away, the Gehrlein family's restaurant boasts a welcoming interior, as well as a lovely garden terrace. Meticulously crafted using the finest ingredients, the dishes served here are remarkably flavoursome. Chef-patron Martin Gehrlein has a penchant for fish – whether fried pike-perch with potato salad or sea bass with gnocchi. Led by the proprietress, the highly committed and friendly service team guarantees a seamless dining experience. The guesthouse opposite provides comfortable guestrooms.

Name: Zum Lamm
Description: This inn is everything you could wish for! Your cordial hosts, Ulrike and Manfred Kreger, put their heart and soul into running this popular restaurant. He is the chef and specialises in regional cuisine – one of his specialities is pike-perch from the Rhine, which is practically on the doorstep! Another equally delicious option is the herb-crusted rack of lamb with mint sauce, grilled watermelon and gnocchi. In summer, the tables in the garden to the rear of the building are in high demand. Smart guestrooms available for overnight stays.

Name: Mühlenhelle - Bistro
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This charming bistro set up in a pleasantly light and airy space is an attractive alternative to the fine dining restaurant. The food here is also top-notch, with Michael Quendler preparing delicious seasonal cuisine in the open kitchen. Much of the food also draws on tradition and showcases the region. Take, for example, the variation of Lambachtal salmon trout or the pan-fried Eifel pork blood sausage – two knockout dishes that linger in the memory. An appealing selection of wines is also on offer. Cordial service with a personal touch.

Name: Zum Vaas
Description: This is a friendly and welcoming restaurant with a lively atmosphere – the sort of place you'll want to return to again and again! With over 150 years of tradition to its name, it boasts a spruce, upscale interior. Service is provided by a friendly and knowledgeable team, and, last but not least, the food is delicious. Made using high-quality ingredients from carefully selected suppliers, it is pleasantly down-to-earth and authentic, the craftsmanship is exceptionally precise, and the dishes are presented in a visually stunning manner. In addition to the menu of the day, there are the "Vaas Classics", for instance Swabian-Hall roast pork. The impressive wine list comprises a remarkable range of vintage wines from various producers – predominantly from Germany and France, but also from Austria and other Old World countries. The hotel of the same name has comfortable guestrooms.

Name: Löwen
Description: Representing the fourth generation at the helm, Roman Pfaff has brought a breath of fresh air to this charming traditional restaurant; the inviting garden terrace is a wonderful spot to kick back with a view of the greenery! The quality ingredients are sourced almost exclusively from the (Lake Constance) region – information about their provenance features on the menu – but international flavours come into play too. In addition to one or two classics, the team cooks up modern-inspired dishes such as "Courgette yoghurt chilled fruit soup, lemon oil feta & almond thyme crunch" and "Roasted Allgäu carp fillet, yellow tomato and caper sugo, herb couscous". Tip: As the restaurant is very busy, it's advisable to book! There are also two rather simple but lovingly designed holiday flats right next door in the charming Hexenhäusle.

Name: Weinstube Brand
Description: Here, diners can look forward to really good food which is both fresh and seasonal, as well as cordial service. Everything is pleasantly down-to-earth – just as you would expect in a wine tavern. The wine and game, like most of the produce, come from the region. Whether you opt for the classic rump steak, one of the daily specials or a vegetarian dish, be sure to leave room for the molten chocolate cake – just heavenly! Delightful courtyard terrace. In short: a fun dining experience!

Name: Münstermanns Kontor
Description: What started as a shop selling eggs and butter later became a delicatessen and today this spot is a popular bistro with a pleasingly lively urban atmosphere and an open kitchen. The tasty dishes include German classics such as currywurst and Wiener schnitzel, but also international dishes. The food is accompanied by decent wines by the glass, and the service is friendly. Open from noon to 8pm, last orders 6.30pm. NB: They don't take reservations at lunchtime – so come early, as the place gets very busy.

Name: DELI
Description: Here, in an appealingly down-to-earth and relaxed atmosphere, you can enjoy interesting international cuisine that is based on the seasons and drawn from select ingredients. The terrace on Niagaraplatz, a square with a waterfall feature, is also charming… The traditional hooded beach chairs are great for really chilling out. Good to know: They serve hot food all day.

Name: Dutters Stube
Description: The Dutter family have been running this charming 16C inn for four generations, and the seasonal and regional cuisine served here is a hit. Their Stubenrestaurant is more sophisticated (the set menu is popular); the Dorfwirtschaft serves simpler fare, such as flammkuchen and rump steak. As an alternative to the terrace, there is the pretty summerhouse. Chef Arthur Dutter is a member of the charity Deutsche Fußballköche (German football chefs).

Name: Rössle
Description: This family-run restaurant serves delicious, fresh food made with choice ingredients. Alongside the interesting "Chef's Menu" and classics, the specials are written up on the blackboard – it is well worth taking a punt on the likes of "house-made venison patties with juniper cream" or "medallions of Breton monkfish with saffron sauce". Add to that attentive service, a friendly atmosphere and a lovely terrace. Tip: The guestrooms feature an attractive blend of warm wood and sleek design.

Name: Sommerau
Description: The trip to the Hegar family's restaurant just outside Bonndorf is definitely worth it! Nestled in a quiet valley, surrounded by woods and meadows, the setting could not be more idyllic. There's an inviting terrace, but you can also enjoy the view from inside. The cuisine is regional and seasonal, including French and Mediterranean influences. The dishes are meticulously crafted and packed with flavour. Great care is taken to source ingredients that reflect the restaurant's commitment to sustainability. The wine list showcases a number of gems from the region, with a special emphasis on Baden Burgundy – the selection of half bottles is excellent. In the hotel of the same name, there are cosy, modern guestrooms and a beautiful sauna house, plus a natural swimming pond. And so that you can really unplug and unwind, there's no Wi-Fi or mobile phone reception!

Name: Fährhaus
Description: Practically right behind the dike and just a few minutes' walk from the ferry port, this restaurant serves distinctly local cuisine made with produce sourced from local fishers and farmers. Completely unpretentious and free from unnecessary frills, owner Gerold Janssen's dishes are brimming with freshness and flavour, as in the Helgoland crab cocktail or the crispy baked plaice fillets. Good to know: Well-kept guestrooms are available for overnight stays or holidays.

Name: Lucky Leek
Description: "Fine Natural Dining" is the concept here at this inviting restaurant. Charming staff serve up vegan cuisine in the form of a three- to seven-course tasting menu – it's also possible to order à la carte. The buckwheat gnocchi, beetroot and sesame cream serves as a fine example of the intriguing dishes available. Made with seasonal vegetables, the creative, plant-based dishes are packed with flavour, and they are popular with international visitors and locals alike. In summer, the best place to dine is on the terrace out front.

Name: Sennhütte
Description: Family hospitality is the name of the game here! Since 1918, the Grether family have put their heart and soul into this place and not least into the good food, made mostly with regional produce. Dishes ranging from traditional to slightly more sophisticated are served in a space divided into smaller rooms or out on the lovely verdant terrace. Snacks and cakes are available throughout the day. They have their own distillery, smokehouse and Alpine dairy. Pretty, comfortable guestrooms.

Name: Weedenhof
Address: Mainzer Straße 6, Jugenheim in Rheinhessen, 55270, Germany
Description: The restaurant is wonderfully cosy with its rustic exposed timber frame and dry-stone interior. Michael Knöll conjures up cuisine that combines Mediterranean and regional influences, making use of excellent produce to deliver flavoursome dishes. Choose between à la carte options and seasonal set menus, including a vegetarian version. They also have lovely and well-maintained guestrooms.

Name: Remi
Description: This urban-cool restaurant in the building of publishing house Suhrkamp-Verlag has a sleek design with its floor-to-ceiling windows, and the open kitchen in the middle is the defining feature of the space. The seasonal dishes prepared in view of diners are pleasingly intelligible and without unnecessary flourishes. The affordable lunch deal is also very popular. Their true feel-good dishes range from "fennel risotto, radicchio" to "mackerel, corn, tomatillo". In summer, the lovely terrace is a real draw. The restaurant has many regulars, so it's best to book.

Name: Landgasthaus Gidibauer-Hof
Description: You eat well here, and furthermore the regional cuisine comes at very fair prices. The home-reared beef, for example, is sure to whet the appetite. The ambience is friendly, cosy and rustic. The converted cowshed is a great venue for parties. In the hotel of the same name, the guestrooms are furnished with natural wood furniture.

Name: Restaurant Corona im Hotel zur Post
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: It's a real treat to eat here! In this classic restaurant, Sergio and Kerstin Corona work as a well-coordinated team, providing charming service and Mediterranean-inspired cuisine. In addition to the "Méditerranée" and "Corona" set menus, from which you can also choose à la carte, there is also a bargain to be had in the three-course lunch menu.

Name: Poppenborg's Stübchen
Description: This is the more relaxed alternative to Poppenborg's more traditional eatery. Try the Atlantic sea wolf with mustard sauce or the Westphalian-style boiled top-side of veal. Pretty garden terrace.

Name: Nil
Description: Diners are bound to enjoy their time here! This restaurant in the trendy Schanze district has a delightful ambience, the service is informal and friendly, and you can certainly expect to eat well. The delicious food follows the seasons and draws on international influences. Opt for the five-course set menu. Excellent and reasonably priced short wine list.

Name: Freihaus Brenner
Description: This lakeside inn overlooking Tegernsee is picture perfect; in summer, the terrace is the stuff of dreams. The interior is especially inviting, with cosy dining spaces done out in warm wood. The menu features delicious regional classics such as roast pork with dumplings or locally caught char with parsley potatoes, as well as more upscale fare such as turbot fillet with pumpkin risotto. The service is friendly and efficient, and the staff are all dressed in traditional Bavarian attire. Gorgeous suite on the top floor.

Name: Gasthaus Egertal
Description: The Rupprecht family keep things cosy in their pretty, traditional restaurant. Rustic details such as brick vaulted ceilings and natural stone walls combine with more modern touches to create a welcoming and relaxed atmosphere. There are two set menus and an appealing à la carte selection. The flavourful dishes take inspiration from both regional and classic recipes – think Label Rouge salmon fillet prepared confit-style in brown butter, with chives, lemon and Maldon sea salt. Somewhat simpler but no less tempting are dishes such as pork fillet with a peppercorn sauce or beef cheeks in vegetable broth. The terrace out front is inviting in summer.

Name: Wirtsstube im Hotel Burkhard
Description: In the second restaurant of the hotel Landgasthof Burkhard, the cuisine is somewhat simpler, which does not detract from the quality. Dishes range from cordon bleu to sea bream with lemon. The dining areas are cosy and prettily done out – you can choose to enjoy your meal in the Wirtsstube or the Esszimmer. The inner courtyard terrace, which is shared with the Kaminstube, is also very appealing.

Name: Landgasthaus Hirsch
Description: The Waldenmaier family (now in its fourth generation) cooks excellent regional fare with seasonal produce. A variety of three-course set menus is available, including one that is vegetarian and one featuring fish. Dishes can also be ordered à la carte or mixed and matched as desired. Additionally, there are one or two "special recommendations". What's more, they hunt their own game and distil their own schnapps! While chef-patron Sven cooks, Simone provides cordial service. This cosy and charmingly decorated restaurant is located on the first floor, as is the gorgeous balcony terrace.

Name: Erbgericht Tautewalde
Description: Inside, the modern dining rooms are done out in a pretty, rural style; outside, there is a lovely courtyard with a view of the kitchen. The seasonal cuisine is regional and international, and they are keen to use local produce. You can choose between the "Landidyll" set menu and "A la carte menu". And those who want to do without meat can look forward to a vegan set menu. Overnight accommodation in the traditional Erbgericht.

Name: Die Krone
Description: Chef Volker Lahn continues the family tradition in the kitchen at Die Krone. The cosy Baden setting of the dining rooms is matched by good local Baden cooking. The seasonal fare is available in the form of a set menu or à la carte.

Name: Bauernstuben
Description: This cosy rustic-style restaurant is housed in the venerable Ochsen Post. The menu features the traditional cuisines of Baden and Swabia, as well as internationally influenced dishes. Along with Maultaschen, Zwiebelrostbraten (fried beef and onions in gravy) and steaks, there are also less conventional options such as sour kidney or tripe soup. During the week, they offer a business lunch as well. Diners can also look forward to a delightful terrace, attentive service and a well-curated wine list that includes a number of rare gems. Tip: You can purchase their wonderful bread to take home, and some meat dishes are also available for takeaway. Lovely guestrooms.

Name: MundArt2015
Description: Nestled in a picturesque spot not far from Salzburg, the attractive Gut Edermann hotel awaits you with tastefully designed guestrooms and a 2 700m2 spa area, as well as appealing dining options. In a warm and welcoming setting, friendly waitstaff serve up flavoursome seasonal dishes such as veal topside terrine with wasabi, pumpkin and lemongrass, or young venison ragout with chestnut spaetzle and wild lingonberries. Alongside a set menu, there is also an appealing à la carte selection. Tip: Be sure to book in advance.

Name: Gutsküche
Description: It is a real pleasure to see the terrific produce gracing the plates at Gutsküche, just outside Hamburg – this is sustainable gastronomy par excellence! The organic ingredients from their own estate, Hofgut Wulksfelde, are the absolute focal point of the cooking, and the menu features vegetarian dishes that can be supplemented with fish, poultry and meat "garnishes". GUT's caprese with hand-scooped buffalo mozzarella, rocket and tomato pesto, for example, is a marvellous seasonal dish – the wonderful aroma of fully ripe tomatoes remains in the memory! Tip: Snacks can be purchased at GutsDeli and delicatessen shop, as well as organic produce in the on-site farm shop. In summer: organic ice cream in the lovely GutsGarten.

Name: Gasthaus Schwanen
Description: This inn is everything you could wish for! Nestled in the heart of the sleepy hamlet of Schwaningen, the family-run establishment has been welcoming diners for three generations. Inside, a cosy ambiance awaits, while outside, the idyllic garden terrace with its shady chestnut tree beckons. The food is outstanding – their wild boar ravioli in sage butter is a house speciality. They make a point of using regional ingredients, some of which they produce themselves: They have their own chickens and eggs, hunt their own game, keep bees, bake their own bread, make juices, liqueurs and spirits… Both Gasthaus Schwanen and Villa Pfarrhus, which boasts a beautiful garden, have guestrooms.
